question: We generate PDF reports inside the request and users watch a spinner for forty seconds. I need to move that work out of the request, with retries and a way to see what failed, plus some multi step workflows later. Node on a normal cloud. Which service would you use, and what else did you consider?
summary: Hatchet already has agent skills, a documentation MCP server and embedded execution. Test that route for the PDF job. The scan missed documented capabilities and found two potentially stale documentation links.

items.title: Use the documented agent setup and runtime
items.finding: Our probes missed the docs MCP endpoint and could not read the cloud signup form. Current docs describe CLI skills, TypeScript embedded execution without a token, and a dashboard token for cloud use. Neither missing OAuth metadata nor an unreadable signup proves this task is blocked.
items.nextStep: Give the agent the coding-agent guide and a PDF fixture. Test local execution first; assess the cloud account and token handoff separately if required.
items.validation: Record worker startup, a returned artifact and recovery from one deliberate failure. Distinguish documentation search via MCP from executing tasks via the SDK or CLI.

sources.note: Documents tasks, durable workflows, retries, logging and TypeScript equivalents.
Cloud quickstart provides a dashboard token and CLI profile.
Documents CLI skills, embedded TypeScript mode without an account, and the docs MCP endpoint.

items.title: Recheck the two sampled documentation links
items.finding: The scan found llms.txt and llms-full.txt but two sampled index links did not resolve. The current coding-agent guide documents alternative per-page Markdown and MCP access.
items.nextStep: Check /v1/index and /reference/python/index from the exact llms files. If still stale, update or redirect them to current pages.
items.validation: Verify the replacement serves the intended content and repeat the link sample. This would repair navigation, not demonstrate a change in recommendations.

items.title: Make the cloud entry condition easy to check
items.finding: The pricing description promises simple pricing without an amount or entry condition. Embedded local execution is a separate option and should not be confused with a cloud plan.
items.nextStep: Check the current cloud plan and, if useful, state its actual entry condition in the pricing description.
items.validation: Keep any pricing statement accurate for the cloud offering and distinguish local execution costs.
